# GriefPrevention3D v19.0.7

**Wiki:** https://github.com/castledking/GriefPrevention3D/wiki

Back up `GriefPreventionData` before updating.

## Vehicle damage: container trust parity & configurable build trust

Breaking vehicles (minecarts, boats) in claims has been aligned with upstream GriefPrevention's
anti-theft behavior, with a configurable option to enforce build trust.

- **Container trust default:** By default, breaking vehicles in a claim requires container trust
  (`/containertrust`), restoring 1:1 parity with upstream GriefPrevention. Players granted container
  trust can break and pick up vehicles in the claim.
- **`Claims.VehiclesRequireBuildTrust: false` (default):** Added to both Paper and Fabric `config.yml`.
  When set to `true`, breaking vehicles in a claim requires build trust (`/trust`), protecting
  minecarts and boats on servers that grant container trust broadly (such as public shops or loot warps).

## Config

New key added to `config.yml` on Paper and Fabric:

```yaml
GriefPrevention:
  Claims:
    VehiclesRequireBuildTrust: false
```

## Upgrade notes

- Restart the server after replacing the jar.
- Both platforms continue to ship in one universal `GriefPrevention3D.jar`: Spigot/Paper/Purpur/Folia
  (1.8 through modern) and Fabric (1.21.2 through 1.21.11, and 26.1 through 26.3). Fabric requires Fabric API.
- No database migrations are required.

# GriefPrevention3D v19.0.6

**Wiki:** https://github.com/castledking/GriefPrevention3D/wiki

Back up `GriefPreventionData` before updating.

## Fabric: Restore Nature

The Restore Nature feature has been ported to Fabric, bringing full parity with Paper and Spigot
for repairing griefed terrain and returning areas to their natural state.

- **`/restorenature`** (`/rn`, `/aclaim restore`): Switches the golden shovel into restoration mode.
  Right-clicking a block inspects and restores a 5-block radius column (from the world's minimum to
  maximum height) back to natural terrain.
- **`/restorenatureaggressive`** (`/rna`, `/aclaim restore aggressive`): Switches to aggressive restoration
  mode. In addition to standard cleanup, this mode overrides claim boundaries, strips player-placed
  ores and bedrock, and clears tree canopies (leaves and logs).
- **`/restorenaturefill [radius]`** (`/rnf`, `/aclaim restore fill [radius]`): Switches to fill mode with
  a custom radius between 1 and 10 blocks (default 2), filling holes and hollowed areas in the terrain.
- **`/basicclaims`** (`/bc`): Exits any active restoration mode and returns the shovel back to standard claim
  creation.

### Restoration behavior

- **Asynchronous column scan:** Terrain processing runs off the main thread. It samples the entire vertical
  column, strips player-placed blocks (such as chests, crafting tables, furnaces, doors, rails, wool,
  planks, slabs, stairs, and torches), removes floating blocks (suspended dirt, snow, or logs), and knocks
  down thin unnatural walls.
- **Natural fill and surface repair:** Terrain holes beneath the surface level are filled in using the
  dimension's base material (netherrack in the Nether, end stone in the End, dirt in the Overworld).
  The natural surface block (grass block, sand, red sand, or mycelium) is restored based on the biome.
- **Claim respect:** Standard restoration skips any block located within an existing claim. Aggressive mode
  can modify claimed blocks.
- **Entity protection:** Players and animals standing within the restoration zone have air cleared at their
  feet and head to prevent suffocation. Unprotected item drops and hanging entities (item frames, paintings)
  in the zone are removed.
- **Visual boundary:** After restoration completes on the server, a 5-second glowing boundary preview
  with lime glazed terracotta corner markers and emerald side markers (matching Paper) outlines the restored
  zone for the user.

### New Fabric commands & permissions

| Command | Permission | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/restorenature` (`/rn`, `/aclaim restore`) | `griefprevention.restorenature` | op | Switches the shovel tool to standard restoration mode |
| `/restorenatureaggressive` (`/rna`, `/aclaim restore aggressive`) | `griefprevention.restorenatureaggressive` | op | Switches the shovel tool to aggressive restoration mode |
| `/restorenaturefill [radius]` (`/rnf`, `/aclaim restore fill [radius]`) | `griefprevention.restorenatureaggressive` | op | Switches the shovel tool to fill mode with radius 1–10 |
| `/gpglow [on\|off\|toggle]` (`/claimglow`) | `griefprevention.visualize` | all | Toggles glowing boundary visualization on or off |

## Boundary visualizations: `/gpglow` toggle & surface fixes

- **`/gpglow toggle` on Fabric and Paper:** Fabric now supports `/gpglow` (`/claimglow`) to enable or
  disable glowing boundary display entities (`/gpglow [on|off|toggle]`). The setting is persisted to
  `Visualizations.Glow` in `config.yml` while preserving comments, and toggling it off immediately despawns
  active glowing entities. Paper's `/gpglow` command handler now also accepts `/gpglow toggle` directly.
- **Single green glow & consistent blocks:** Aligned Fabric restore nature markers with Paper, using
  `lime_glazed_terracotta` corners and `emerald_block` sides with a single green glow outline (`0x55FF55`)
  instead of separate aqua and green glows.

...

releases.notes:
# GriefPrevention3D v19.0.5

**Wiki:** https://github.com/castledking/GriefPrevention3D/wiki

Back up `GriefPreventionData` before updating.

## Faster large shaped claims

Large shaped edits could stall the server or consume excessive memory while extending a path
around an existing claim. Several calculations scanned every block column inside the shape's
bounding rectangle, even when most of that rectangle was outside the claim.

- **Shape unions, cuts, overlap checks and containment checks use compact ranges.** They no longer
  need to allocate a point for every claimed column or walk the entire bounding rectangle.
- **Path extensions and claim merges use the same optimized geometry on Bukkit/Paper and Fabric.**
  Merge-corridor width and connectivity checks also avoid block-by-block flood fills.
- **Shaped subdivision checks remain exact.** Concave gaps stay outside the claim, and rectangular
  subdivisions only one block wide still work inside shaped parents.
- **Claims already at their minimum depth skip the automatic depth scan on Bukkit/Paper.** This
  avoids collecting potentially thousands of chunk snapshots when no downward extension is possible.

A regression benchmark uses a real 427-corner coastline covering about 1.56 million block columns.
Joining it to a large rectangle took approximately **15 ms** with the new geometry; the previous
routine exhausted the same **192 MiB test heap**. This measures the geometry calculation, not a
complete live-server interaction or the work performed by other plugins.

## Editable tutorial links

The survival, creative and subdivision tutorial links can now be changed separately from their
surrounding messages. All 16 bundled message files include these entries:

```yaml
Messages:
  SurvivalVideoURL: '&3&nbit.ly/mcgpuser&r'
  CreativeVideoURL: '&3&nbit.ly/mcgpcrea&r'
  SubdivisionVideoURL: '&3&nbit.ly/mcgpsub&r'
```

On Bukkit/Paper, edit the active file in `plugins/GriefPreventionData/Lang/messages_<locale>.yml`.
On Fabric, edit `plugins/GriefPreventionData/messages.yml`. Replace the default links with your own
URLs and run `/gpreload` after saving. Color codes are supported.

The configured links are used by the corresponding tutorial prompts and, on Bukkit/Paper, the
survival welcome book. With per-player locales enabled on Bukkit/Paper, the URL follows the
player's language file. Existing books already in inventories are not rewritten.

Keep `{0}` in `SurvivalBasicsVideo2`, `CreativeBasicsVideo2`, `SubdivisionVideo2` and `BookLink`
where the link should appear. Existing customized help text is preserved.

## Upstream cleanup

Synced upstream's removal of obsolete config, numeric material-ID and claim-filename migration
helpers. Unrecognized files in `ClaimData` are now skipped and logged rather than deleted or
automatically renamed. Very old installations that still need those conversions should first
upgrade through a release that provides them.

## Upgrade notes

- Restart the server after replacing the jar. `/gpreload` applies later message-file edits.
- The new message keys are added with the existing tutorial URLs as defaults. No new config
  options or permission nodes are required.
- Current claim files keep the same format; existing shaped claims benefit without being redrawn.
- Both platforms continue to ship in one universal `GriefPrevention3D.jar`. Fabric requires Fabric API.

# GriefPrevention3D v19.0.4

**Wiki:** https://github.com/castledking/GriefPrevention3D/wiki

Back up `GriefPreventionData` before updating.

## Admin claim trust under `RequireIgnoreClaimsInAdminClaims`

When `GriefPrevention.RequireIgnoreClaimsInAdminClaims: true` is enabled on Spigot or Paper,
staff holding `griefprevention.adminclaims` are no longer blocked before GP3D checks the claim's
trust list:

- **Claim trust works without `/ignoreclaims`.** Public grants such as `/containertrust public`
  (including trading with villagers and opening public containers), personal trust, and permission
  trust now apply to staff the same way they apply to any other player.
- **Untrusted build and container actions still require `/ignoreclaims`.** Actions not covered by
  the claim's trust list continue to return the normal denial message with the `/ignoreclaims`
  reminder.
- **Administrative subdivisions follow the same rule.** Administrative subdivisions inside player
  claims now enforce `RequireIgnoreClaimsInAdminClaims` for build and container checks unless the
  action is covered by trust on the subdivision (or inherited from an unrestricted parent claim).
  Walking through, resizing, and managing trust in administrative subdivisions still work without
  `/ignoreclaims`.

## Upgrade notes

- Only servers with `GriefPrevention.RequireIgnoreClaimsInAdminClaims: true` (off by default) are
  affected.
- No config or data changes are required, and Fabric behavior is unchanged.
- Both platforms continue to ship in one universal `GriefPrevention3D.jar`. Fabric requires Fabric API.

# GriefPrevention3D v19.0.3

**Wiki:** https://github.com/castledking/GriefPrevention3D/wiki

Back up `GriefPreventionData` before updating.

## Prevent climbing on rejected blocks

Players can sometimes use a client-predicted block as a temporary step even though GP3D rejects
its placement in a claim. This release adds an optional setback to prevent repeated placements
from being used to climb walls. It is available on Bukkit/Paper and Fabric.

The option is **off by default**. To enable it, add or change this setting in
`plugins/GriefPreventionData/config.yml`:

```yaml
GriefPrevention:
  Claims:
    PreventBlockPlaceClimbing: true
```

Run `/gpreload` after saving. When GP3D denies a colliding placement near a player's feet, the
protection can return them to a recent position supported by real blocks, including when the
upward movement arrives after the placement is denied. The destination is checked for support
and clearance before a setback.

Ordinary jumps, authorized building, active claim bypass, flying, gliding, swimming and vehicle
movement are unaffected. A recent safe position is needed before a setback can occur.

## Upgrade notes

- Existing servers keep their previous behavior until the new setting is enabled.
- No new permission nodes are required.
- Both platforms continue to ship in one universal `GriefPrevention3D.jar`. Fabric requires Fabric API.

# GriefPrevention3D v19.0.2

**Wiki:** https://github.com/castledking/GriefPrevention3D/wiki

Back up `GriefPreventionData` before updating.

## Weaving protection on Paper and Fabric

Weaving could create cobwebs inside another player's claim when an affected player or mob died. This update
protects those placements on Paper, Purpur, Folia and Fabric.

- **Player deaths require build trust.** Every prospective cobweb is checked at the block where it would
  appear. Dying outside a claim can no longer place webs across its boundary. Subdivision restrictions and
  3D height boundaries are respected, and authorized claim bypass still works.
- **Mob deaths cannot place cobwebs inside claims.** The death does not reliably identify who applied the
  weaving effect, so claimed blocks are protected regardless of the mob's type. Weaving still works in
  survival wilderness and in worlds where claims are disabled.
- **Claimed animals and villagers require container trust to receive weaving potions.** Access trust alone
  is insufficient. This covers splash potions and both standard and custom lingering weaving effects.
- **Dispensers cannot apply weaving across claim boundaries.** They may affect creatures in the same claim
  as the dispenser, including the same subdivision. A neighboring claim is treated separately even when it
  has the same owner. Fabric remembers the dispenser's launch location and carries it into the lingering
  cloud, so the potion's landing position cannot bypass this check.

Players may still drink weaving potions and receive their own thrown potion effects. Any cobwebs generated
by their death follow the build-permission checks above. Other potion effects are unchanged.

The Fabric protection runs in both bundled adapters, covering Minecraft 1.21.2–1.21.11 and 26.1–26.3.

## Upstream updates

- Removed the obsolete conversion of player names to UUIDs, following upstream GriefPrevention. MySQL
  support and migration from flat files to the database remain available in GP3D.
- Synced upstream's knockback-listener cleanup. GP3D retains its existing handling, which already avoids
  processing the same entity knockback twice.

## Upgrade notes

- No new config keys or permission nodes are needed. Existing claims, trust and UUID-based data keep working.
- **Mob-based cobweb farms inside claims will stop placing webs.** Mob-generated cobwebs remain allowed in
  survival wilderness; player-generated webs in claims require build trust.
- Servers whose GP data still uses pre-UUID player names must first update through an older release that
  performs that conversion, then update to 19.0.2.

Both platforms continue to ship in one universal `GriefPrevention3D.jar`. Fabric requires Fabric API.

releases.notes:
# GriefPrevention3D v19.0.1

**Wiki:** https://github.com/castledking/GriefPrevention3D/wiki

Back up `GriefPreventionData` before updating.

## Fabric: inactive players' claims expire

Fabric used to ignore `Claims.Expiration`. It now cleans up claims as the plugin does, so abandoned claims no
longer pile up on long-running servers.

- **`Claims.Expiration.AllClaims.DaysInactive`** (60 days by default) deletes all of a player's claims once they
  have been away that long.
- **`Claims.Expiration.ChestClaimDays`** (7 days by default) deletes a player's only claim sooner, if it is no
  bigger than a new player's claim (`Claims.AutomaticNewPlayerClaimsRadius`, 4 by default, a 9×9 claim). With
  Fabric's default minimum area of 100 blocks, few claims are that small.
- As on the plugin, one claim owner is checked every `Advanced.ClaimExpirationCheckRate` seconds (60 by default),
  going round every owner in turn.

These players keep their claims:

- anyone online;
- anyone with at least `ExceptWhenOwnerHasTotalClaimBlocks` claim blocks (10000 by default), or at least
  `ExceptWhenOwnerHasBonusClaimBlocks` bonus blocks (5000 by default);
- anyone with **`griefprevention.dontexpire`**.

`griefprevention.dontexpire` works with LuckPerms even while the player is offline: their LuckPerms data is loaded
for the check and released afterwards, so a grant on a group they belong to counts too. Without LuckPerms, server
operators are exempt, which is the permission's default. If the check fails, the claims stay.

Expired claims are deleted without the `AbandonReturnRatio` penalty, and each one is written to the server log.
Other Fabric mods can keep a claim from expiring through the new `ClaimExpirationCallback`, as plugins can with
`ClaimExpirationEvent`.

### When the first claims can expire

Fabric learns when players were last online from `GriefPreventionData/LastSeen.yml`, which started recording in
18.4.7 (26 September 2026). Players not seen since then keep their claims, as the plugin keeps the claims of
players without a last-played time. With the default 60 days, no claim can expire before late November 2026.

### New command

| Command | Permission | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/checkclaimexpiry [player]` (`/claimcheckexpiry`, `/aclaim checkexpiry`) | `griefprevention.checkclaimexpiry` | Shows when the owner of the claim you stand in was last seen, when their claims expire, and what keeps them |

Checking another player by name also takes `griefprevention.admin.checkclaimexpiry`, which only operators have by
default, as on the plugin.

## Spigot and Paper

- **Indonesian messages.** Set `GriefPrevention.Locale` to `id_ID`, or let `PerPlayerLocale` pick it for players
  whose client is set to Bahasa Indonesia.
- bStats now reports the server software by its name (for example Paper or Purpur), from upstream GriefPrevention
  (#2667).

## Config

New Fabric `config.yml` keys, matching the plugin. They are added to existing files on startup without changing
anything you have set, and `/gpreload` rereads them:

```yaml
GriefPrevention:
  Claims:
    AutomaticNewPlayerClaimsRadius: 4
    Expiration:
      ChestClaimDays: 7
      AllClaims:
        DaysInactive: 60
        ExceptWhenOwnerHasTotalClaimBlocks: 10000
        ExceptWhenOwnerHasBonusClaimBlocks: 5000
  Advanced:
    ClaimExpirationCheckRate: 60
```

## Upgrade notes

- **Expiration is on by default on Fabric**, as on the plugin. To keep every claim, set both `DaysInactive` and
  `ChestClaimDays` to `0`.
- If a Fabric expiration setting cannot be read, expiration turns off and the error is logged, instead of falling
  back to the defaults.
- `Claims.Expiration.UnusedClaimDays` and `AutomaticNatureRestoration` are not on Fabric yet. Both need restore
  nature, which Fabric does not have.

Both versions still ship in one `GriefPrevention3D.jar`: 1.8 through the latest release on Spigot, Paper, Purpur
and Folia, and 1.21.2 through 1.21.11 and 26.1 through 26.3 on Fabric.

# GriefPrevention3D v19.0.0

**Now a stable build.** One universal JAR runs as a Bukkit plugin and as a Fabric dedicated-server mod. Fabric
requires Fabric API. Back up `GriefPreventionData` before updating.

## Fabric claims and commands

- **Create and manage claims.** Basic and administrative claims, 2D and 3D subdivisions, claim lookup, abandonment,
  trust, trust lists, and staff claim management are available through the same command aliases and permission nodes
  as the plugin. Fabric has no economy integration, so paid claim transfers are refused unless the player has the
  free-transfer permission.
- **Shaped claims.** Enable `GriefPrevention.Claims.AllowShapedClaims`, then use `/shapedclaims` (alias
  `/shapedclaim` or `/claim mode shaped`). With the golden shovel, right-click the outline's corners in order and
  click the first corner again to close it. The live path and finished claim both show corner nibs and boundary
  markers. Clicking an existing 2D claim boundary starts a reshape.
- **Extend claims.** `/extendclaim <numberOfBlocks>` (aliases `/expandclaim` and `/resizeclaim`) extends or shrinks
  the most specific claim at your location, or the claim selected with the shovel nib. It supports 2D and 3D claims,
  subdivisions, and shaped outlines.
- **Inspect claims.** The configured investigation tool (`STICK` by default) shows the claim at the targeted block;
  sneak-use it to visualize nearby claims. The golden shovel displays claim boundaries and supports claim selection.
- **Resize with the scroll wheel.** `/scrollresize` previews a claim or subdivision while scrolling and applies the
  change on right-click. Looking down selects the bottom face of a 3D subdivision. A selected corner is range-gated
  to avoid a corner click registering through to a farther block.

Shaped claims are disabled by default. `AllowShapedSubClaims` also defaults to `false`; `ShapedMinimumWidth` and
`ShapedMinimumArea` control their size rules. `Allow3DSubdivisions` defaults to `true`. These settings are read from
the existing `config.yml` and added on startup when missing.

## Claim protection

- Explosions respect the configured land-claim and surface explosion protections, including protected entities.
- Starting or extending a raid requires build trust in the raid-center claim, or in the triggering player's claim
  when the raid center is unclaimed. `Claims.RaidTriggersRequireBuildTrust` defaults to `true`.

## Compatibility and packaging

- One Modrinth release lists Bukkit, Folia, Paper, Purpur, Spigot, and Fabric, using this combined changelog.
- Fabric supports Minecraft 1.21.2–1.21.11 and 26.1–26.3 on dedicated servers. Bukkit-family support starts at
  Minecraft 1.8.
- The universal JAR is about 2.2 MB, below the 5 MB target.

## Upgrade notes

No claim migration is needed. Existing settings remain in place; new config keys are added with the defaults above.
